TORONTO, Nov. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Partners Value Investments Inc. (the “Company”, TSXV: PVF.PR.V, PVF.A) announced today its financial results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026. All amounts are stated in United States dollars ("US dollars").

For the three months ended September 30, 2026, the Company recorded net income of $564 million, compared to a net loss of $2,188 million in the prior year period. The increase in net income was primarily due to remeasurement gains of $476 million associated with the Company's retractable common shares, remeasurement gains of $70 million associated with the Company's exchangeable shares and nil warrant liability remeasurement gains (losses) in the current period, compared to remeasurement losses of $1,898 million, $76 million and $252 million associated with the Company's retractable common shares, exchangeable shares and warrants, respectively, in the prior year period. The increase was partially offset by foreign currency translation losses of $1 million compared to foreign currency translation gains of $15 million in the prior year period.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company recorded net income of $1,316 million, compared to a net loss of $1,351 million in the prior year period. The increase in net income was primarily due to remeasurement gains of $1,062 million, $71 million and $109 million associated with the Company's retractable common shares, exchangeable shares and warrants, respectively, and foreign currency translation gains of $32 million in the current period, compared to remeasurement losses of $1,192 million, $56 million and $136 million associated with the Company's retractable common shares, exchangeable shares and warrants, respectively, and foreign currency translation losses of $24 million in the prior year period.

The Company's retractable common shares, exchangeable shares and warrants are classified as liabilities due to their retractable, exchangeable and convertible features, respectively. The remeasurement gains or losses on retractable common shares and exchangeable shares in a given period are driven by the respective depreciation or appreciation of the Partners Value Investments L.P.'s Equity LP unit ("Equity LP unit") price. The remeasurement gains or losses on warrants in a given period are driven by the respective depreciation or appreciation of the market price of a warrant. The Company's outstanding warrants expired on June 30, 2026, in accordance with the warrant terms.

Adjusted Earnings is a non-IFRS measure that can be used to evaluate the performance of the Company, defined as net income (loss) attributable to the Company, excluding the impact of remeasurement gains (losses) on retractable common shares, exchangeable shares, and warrant liability, as well as dividends paid on retractable common shares.

Adjusted Earnings for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $25 million, compared to Adjusted Earnings of $46 million in the prior year period. The decrease in Adjusted Earnings was primarily due to foreign currency translation losses, lower valuation gains on our investment portfolio, higher preferred share dividends and higher current tax expense, partially offset by higher investment income and deferred tax recovery.

Adjusted Earnings for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $96 million, compared to Adjusted Earnings of $55 million in the prior year period. The increase in Adjusted Earnings was primarily due to higher investment income, foreign currency translation gains, and deferred tax recovery, partially offset by net investment valuation losses, higher preferred share dividends, and higher current tax expense.

3Notice has no immediate listing or trading effectTrading continues for now, but failure to cure may lead to delisting.
4An additional 180-day period may be availableEligibility depends on meeting other listing standards, including $1M market value of publicly held shares.

data.title: NuRAN Wireless Receives Nasdaq Notification Regarding Minimum Bid Price Deficiency
data.description:
QUEBEC, QC / ACCESS Newswire / November 13, 2026 / NuRAN Wireless Inc. ("NuRAN" or the "Company"), a provider of rural connectivity infrastructure in Africa, today announces that on November 10, 2026, it received a written notification letter (the "Notification Letter") from the Nasdaq Stock Market LLC ("Nasdaq") notifying NuRAN that it was not in compliance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2), as the minimum bid price of the Company's common shares ("Shares") has been below US$1.00 per share for 30 consecutive business days.

The Notification Letter is only a notification of deficiency and not a notice of delisting. As such, the Notification Letter has no immediate effect on the listing or trading of the Company's Shares on the Nasdaq Capital Market under the symbol "NUR."

Nasdaq Listing Rules

Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2) requires securities listed on the Nasdaq Capital Market to maintain a minimum bid price of US$1.00 per share, and Listing Rule 5810(c)(3)(A) provides that a failure to meet the minimum bid price requirement exists if the deficiency continues for a period of 30 consecutive business days. Based on the closing bid price of the Company's Shares for the 30 consecutive business days from September 29, 2026, to November 9, 2026, the Company has not met the minimum bid price requirement.

In accordance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5810(c)(3)(A), NuRAN has a period of 180 calendar days, or until May 10, 2027, to regain compliance with the minimum bid price requirement. To regain compliance, the closing bid price of the Company's Shares must meet or exceed US$1.00 for at least ten consecutive business days during this 180-calendar day compliance period. Nasdaq may, in its discretion, require the Company to satisfy the minimum bid price requirement for a period of more than ten consecutive business days, generally not exceeding 20 consecutive business days, before determining that the Company has demonstrated an ability to maintain long-term compliance.

If the Company does not regain compliance by May 10, 2027, it may be eligible for an additional 180-calendar-day compliance period, provided that it meets the continued listing requirement for market value of publicly held shares (US$1 million) and all other initial listing standards for the Nasdaq Capital Market, other than the minimum bid price requirement. The Company must also provide written notice to Nasdaq of its intention to cure the deficiency during the additional compliance period, by effecting a reverse stock split, if necessary. If the Company elects to implement a reverse stock split, Nasdaq requires that it be completed no later than ten business days prior to the expiration of the initial 180-calendar-day compliance period ending May 10, 2027.

If it appears to Nasdaq that NuRAN will not be able to cure the deficiency, or if NuRAN is not otherwise eligible for additional time to regain compliance, the Company's Shares will be subject to delisting by Nasdaq. NuRAN may appeal any Nasdaq determination to delist its Shares, and during any appeal process, the Company's Shares would continue to trade on the Nasdaq Capital Market.

NuRAN's management intends to actively monitor the bid price for its Shares and will consider all available options to regain compliance with the Nasdaq minimum bid price requirement.

The Company's business operations are not affected by the receipt of the Notification Letter.

About NuRAN Wireless

NuRAN Wireless Inc. is a rural telecommunications infrastructure company connecting remote and underserved communities across Africa. Through its Network-as-a-Service model, NuRAN finances, builds, owns, operates and maintains 2G, 3G and 4G mobile network infrastructure for mobile network operators seeking to expand coverage outside urban markets.

NuRAN is also building on this foundation through NuEnergy, its wholly owned subsidiary focused on owning and operating the Company's solar, storage and hybrid power systems across its African footprint.

data.title: More Than 10,000 Flights Delayed or Canceled in FAA's Nationwide Groundstop— WSJ
data.description:
By Andrew Tangel, Jacob Passy and Alison Sider

The Federal Aviation Administration halted departing flights nationwide Friday afternoon, citing extraordinary circumstances and safety concerns after air-traffic control communications were disrupted.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy wrote on X that there had been a communication issue affecting multiple air route traffic-control centers, which handle high-altitude flights covering large swaths of the country. "FAA technicians are investigating the issue," he wrote.

Planes in the air are able to continue flying to their destinations, an FAA spokeswoman said. Inbound international flights will be managed on a case-by-case basis, the agency said.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters at the White House on Friday that "there was no prior indication, or indication as of yet, that this was a nefarious attack against us. This is a telecommunications outage as of now." When asked if it could be a cyberattack, Mullin said officials weren't ruling anything out yet.

"There's no reason for the public to be afraid or scared for your loved ones," Mullin said, adding this isn't "another 9/11."

The groundstop started Friday afternoon at 3:53 p.m. ET. More than 1,100 U.S. flights had been canceled and nearly 10,000 had been delayed as of Friday at 5:40 p.m. ET, according to FlightAware. As of around 4 p.m., there were still roughly 11,000 flights scheduled to depart from U.S. airports Friday, according to aviation analytics company Cirium.

Disruptions are likely to grow. With departures halted, airports fill up, leaving little room for more flights to land. Nearly 500 flights returned to the airport they took off from as of 5:50 pm ET Friday, and more than 100 diverted to another airport, according to Cirium, an aviation analytics firm.

That leaves planes and crew members out of place for their next flights, which could create cascading scheduling problems into the weekend.

Some international departures from the east and west coasts were being allowed to take off Friday evening, according to industry officials.

At Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, word quickly spread among travelers while ground traffic appeared to suddenly stop on the tarmac late Friday afternoon. By early evening, telecom issues at some FAA air-traffic facilities were coming back online, according to people familiar with the matter.

The outage appears to be affecting a telecommunications network overseen by L3Harris Technologies, according to people briefed on the matter. The network handles crucial radio frequencies that air-traffic controllers use to communicate with pilots, the people said. It wasn't immediately clear whether the outage also affected the radar feeds that controllers use to keep aircraft safely separated in the skies.

An L3Harris spokeswoman didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

United Airlines said it is responding to the groundstop and will work with customers to get them to destinations once the issue is resolved. American said it expects its schedule to be disrupted for the rest of the day, depending how long the groundstop remains in place.

"It will be all hands on deck across American to get customers on their way as soon as possible when the FAA lifts this ground stop," American said in a statement.

Several airlines issued waivers to allow travelers to rebook flights without penalty. At some airports, including New York's LaGuardia, travelers whose flights were cancelled had to wait in long lines to get their checked bags back before they could go home. At Newark Liberty International Airport in New Jersey, security lines were empty as people milled about checking their phones for updates.

John Sturino, a musician who plays the drums, said he is going to miss a percussion convention in Indianapolis because of the flight delay. The Brooklyn native said he had been waiting half an hour in line to cancel his flight at the Delta lounge desk in LaGuardia Airport and get a refund.

"It wasn't worth staying in the airport," he said.

Sara Garven, 66, was traveling with her husband home to Wisconsin from Sarasota, Fla., when the couple were stranded in Baltimore where they had a layover. Overhead announcements were being made roughly every 30 minutes, she said, but the information was no different from what was available online.

"Some are sprinkling the Friday the 13th component, which isn't really helping," she said. "Our main concern is just getting home safely."

This is the second time in recent years the FAA has taken the extraordinary step of halting all departures across the country.

In 2023, a nationwide groundstop was ordered amid an outage of the FAA's Notice to Airmen system, which provides critical information to pilots. That order lasted for two hours, contributing to more than 1,000 flight cancellations. Before that, the FAA had only taken that step on Sept. 11, 2001.

The nation's air-traffic control system has been beset by communications issues leading to radio and radar outages that have affected various FAA facilities in recent years. Earlier this year, flights at New York-area airports were halted when a contractor accidentally cut a fiber communications line in New Jersey.

Other outages that have affected the Dallas area, Upper Midwest and New York City area have been relatively contained.

data.title: The Chaos and Unexpected Joys of a 19-Hour Global Email Outage — WSJ
data.description:
By Robert McMillan and Angel Au-Yeung

We may live in an age of messaging apps and artificial intelligence, but as about half a billion people discovered this week, good old-fashioned email is pretty important, too.

Starting around 12:30 p.m. Eastern on Thursday, a Microsoft cloud outage knocked the company's email and other services offline. The interruption left swaths of the globe, from healthcare systems to stock exchanges to members of U.K. Parliament, without one of their main tools for communicating. It was the tech world's equivalent of a snow day.

The cause was a server upgrade gone wrong, which then cascaded globally. It was a day reminiscent of the chaos caused in 2024 when the cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike crashed 8.5 million Windows systems.

Some users were frustrated. Some simply checked out from work. Others time-traveled back to the telephone era.

Support staff at Envision Technology Advisors, a technical services company, spent yesterday on the phone explaining to customers why their email wasn't working, said Stephen Rose, the company's chief technology officer.

Invision's customers began reaching out early in the day, but with email cut off, they had to turn to the telephone, Rose said. So they called. "Our service desk got totally paralyzed," he said.

Rose's team told callers that Envision wasn't to blame for the outage; Microsoft was. "You hope that it gets out by word of telephone," he said.

Email-deprived entities around the world encouraged customers to reach out via phone, including a water utility in Halifax, Nova Scotia; Detroit's light-rail system; and the East Gippsland region of Australia.

In the U.S., city governments across the country lost email, including Tampa, Fla.; Louisville, Ky.; and the County of Los Angeles Medical Examiner. The House of Representatives was hit too. As was the shipping company Maersk and European exchange operator Euronext. In England, the National Health Service was among several government agencies affected by the outage.

The Lincolnshire Partnership NHS Foundation Trust, a British publicly funded healthcare provider that specializes in mental health services, put out a press release with instructions for patients during the outage. "We would ask that if you need to make a referral today, or you are experiencing a crisis please call our services rather than email at this time," the statement said.

The outage affected a range of Microsoft 365 services, but it centered on Exchange Online and email services, Microsoft said.

Microsoft Teams, a messaging and video chat platform, remained up for many, prompting complaints. "Dear @ Microsoft - you shut down the wrong one. Please turn our email back on and kill Teams. Sincerely, Everyone," wrote Steve Schale, a political strategist based in Florida, on X.

For Jeffrey Michelson, a partner at an accounting firm based in New York City, the outage became a welcome chance to check a few items off his to-do list.

Michelson noticed he wasn't getting any new emails in his inbox in the early afternoon on Thursday. After dropping his daughter off at karate lessons just before sunset, he realized he might not be receiving emails for the rest of the evening.

So he got to work building two bookshelves that his wife had been asking him to complete for a month. "It was kind of nice, I'm not gonna lie," said Michelson. The next day, he woke up in the early morning to 70 unread emails.

Like any snow day, Thursday was fun for some but not so great for people who depended on Microsoft's cloud to get their work done. "Kids love a snow day," Envision's Rose said. "Parents go, 'Oh, my God, I've got these kids inside the house all day.' It's all a matter of perspective."

The outage was more disruptive for some than others. Workhorse Group, an industrial company based in the Detroit area, had to reschedule its third-quarter earnings call to the following week because of the outage.

"Our experience (clearly, like many others) shows how vital it is to have real-time communications, access to documents and the ability to share documents with others," said company spokesman John Williams. He sent his comment via text message.

A Microsoft spokesman said the company wasn't hacked. It was a network upgrade gone wrong, he said. "Given the scale of demand, we restored services gradually, validating stability at each stage. While this took longer, it helped ensure a stable restoration," he said.

The blackout lasted about 19 hours, said Doug Madory, head of internet analysis at the networking company Infoblox.

On X, Microsoft Chief Executive Satya Nadella was silent on the outage. That is not a complete surprise. "I'm an email typist," he told Bloomberg last year.

data.title: SpaceX launches 15th Starship flight with hopes of achieving first round trip
data.description:
Key points:
  • SpaceX plans attempt at first return-landing catch of Starship on Saturday
  • Test is key to Musk's effort to produce fully reusable rocket ship
  • Starship delivering its second batch of satellites to orbit

By Joey Roulette

SpaceX launched the 15th flight of its Starship spacecraft from Texas on Friday on a mission the company hopes will be the first round-trip rocket voyage to orbit and back to the very spot where it left Earth, a key test of Elon Musk's effort to build a fully reusable rocket system.

Plans call for Starship's uncrewed upper-stage vessel to re-enter the atmosphere after nearly a day in orbit and return to its launch tower on Saturday for an engine-controlled touchdown assisted by the giant mechanical arms of a pioneering catch-landing mechanism.

SpaceX had intended to use the same return-flight and "chopstick"-arm technology to recover Starship's lower-stage booster rocket shortly after the two parts of the spacecraft separated within minutes of the launch.

But the Super Heavy booster, for reasons not immediately clear, was diverted from its return flight path to a fixed point over the Gulf of Mexico and momentarily hovered in the air before exploding a short distance over the sea surface.

SpaceX mission controllers hoped to have better luck in steering Starship's upper stage back to home base at the end of its flight. The vehicle reached orbit about 27 minutes after launch, SpaceX said.

KEY TEST OF REUSABILITY

Bringing the top portion of the spacecraft intact back to the platform where it was launched would mark a breakthrough in the ambitions of Musk, who founded SpaceX in 2002, to reduce spaceflight costs by developing a fully recyclable rocket system.

The combined vehicle, consisting of the main Starship cargo-and-crew vessel perched atop its Super Heavy booster rocket and standing 40 stories high, roared off its launch pad from SpaceX's South Texas Starbase complex along the Gulf of Mexico near Brownsville.

The flight marked Starship's 15th test flight since 2023 and the second to carry a batch of operational Starlink satellites to orbit. That makes the mission both a revenue-generating endeavor for SpaceX's satellite-connectivity business and a high-stakes test for a rocket ship still under development.

Starship 15 began releasing its cargo of 26 satellites about 36 minutes into its flight in a payload-delivery operation expected to take less than an hour to complete, the company said in a livestream presentation of the mission.

Musk's space and AI business views Starship as key to expanding its network of Starlink internet satellites and, in the future, deploying a swarm of orbital AI data-processing centers dubbed Starmind, as the company positions itself to become a high-tech infrastructure provider.

SpaceX last launched Starship in September, taking the rocket and a payload of satellites to orbit for the first time despite some rocket engines shutting down mid-flight. That mission, planned to last 10 hours, ended after roughly three hours with an upper stage splashing down intact into the Pacific Ocean before bursting into flames.

RETURN-FLIGHT AND RECOVERY PLANS

For Friday's mission, the company was aiming for both the lower-stage Super Heavy and the upper-stage Starship to return to the spacecraft's Texas launch site for safe landing and recovery. Plans called for the orbital cruise vessel to touch down about 22 hours after launch. SpaceX has said it would be a "breakthrough moment in making Starship a reliable, rapidly reusable rocket" if that feat is achieved.

SpaceX has previously returned the 236-foot (72-meter) Super Heavy booster three times to its launch pad after sending Starship to space, with the booster flying itself back to Earth minutes after launch and gently descending upright into the grasp of a pair of large mechanical arms fixed to the launch tower. The last such "tower catch" was in March 2025.

It was not immediately clear why Friday's attempt failed.

Starship was expected to descend from space after completing 14 orbits around Earth, setting up its debut catch landing for Saturday afternoon.

Musk has said he expects to achieve a pace of weekly Starship launches by the first half of 2027.

NASA has helped fund Starship's development with roughly $3.2 billion since selecting the rocket ship in 2021 to serve as a lunar lander for its astronauts under the multibillion-dollar Artemis moon program. SpaceX has put at least $15 billion of its own funds into the rocket's development.

NASA and SpaceX expect Starship to land humans on the moon by 2028, though several major testing objectives remain that analysts and industry engineers believe will push that timeline back. Those milestones include demonstrating complex fuel transfers between Starship tanker rockets in orbit, a critical process that will enable Starship to travel beyond Earth's orbit to the moon.

Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin is also developing a moon lander, Blue Moon, for NASA under the Artemis program. Blue Moon is poised to join Starship and another spacecraft, NASA's Orion capsule, in Earth's orbit next year for Artemis III, a docking test mission before NASA's planned moon landing missions begin with Artemis IV.

data.title: Costco: An AI Shelter? — Barrons.com

By George Glover

Fears of a slowdown in artificial-intelligence spending have hit the market like a gale-force storm lately. Looking for shelter? Costco Wholesale shares could shield investors from all that volatility.

Late Tuesday, it declared a special cash dividend of $30 — enough to buy you 20 servings of Costco's legendary $1.50 hot dog/soda combo. More good news: Costco also said its board had approved a $4 billion stock buyback program. The market always likes those.

Both developments suggest the stock could be a good defensive play for investors looking for steady returns in these uncertain times. "Strong execution, durable cash generation, and shareholder returns helps explain why investors continue to flock to Costco," Jefferies analyst Corey Tarlowe said in a note.

The results are already in. Hopes of a one-off dividend have helped power the stock 24% higher this year, but even the bulls weren't expecting such a hefty payout. "The special dividend is well above our expectations of about $20 per share," says Oppenheimer's Rupesh Parikh, who has had Costco as a top pick for the past year.

Looking for that rare sort of stock that looks both AI and inflation-proof? You could do a lot worse. And, enjoy the hot dogs.

data.title: Fed's Jefferson: Further Policy Adjustments Should Be Determined By Carefully Examining Trends in the Data
data.description:
By Jessica Coacci

Federal Reserve Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said that further policy adjustments should be determined by carefully examining trends in the data, the evolving outlook, and the balance of risks.

"Data received so far for October remains consistent with well above-target inflation," according to the text of Jefferson's remarks, scheduled to be delivered in San Diego on Friday.

Jefferson said that data received since the Fed's October policy meeting have been consistent with economic activity and labor market conditions remaining broadly solid, while inflation readings show persistent price pressures.

Jefferson also said he remains concerned about the risk of higher energy prices leading to a persistent rise in inflation more broadly.

"Going forward, I believe that further policy adjustments should be determined by carefully examining trends in the data, the evolving outlook, and the balance of risks," Jefferson said.
